candidate.answerReason: Outside the intersection are 2007−1001=1006 elements, split equally between the two sets. Each set therefore contains 503+1001=1504 elements.

methods.label: Separate the common part
methods.explanation:
The \(1001\) elements in the intersection belong to both sets. Removing this common part from the union leaves the elements belonging to exactly one set:
\[
2007-1001=1006.
\]
Because \(A\) and \(B\) have equal sizes and contain the same common part, their parts outside the intersection must also have equal sizes. These two disjoint parts together contain \(1006\) elements, so each contains
\[
1006\div2=503.
\]
Set \(A\) consists of its \(503\) elements outside the intersection together with the \(1001\) common elements. Therefore, its number of elements is
\[
503+1001=\boxed{1504},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\mathrm{C}}\).
